newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rating good for Russia, politics to have last word.
newsitem.headline: Rating good for Russia, politics to have last word.

text.p: Russia's new credit ratings seem likely to push MinFin prices up further and ensure a good reception for its forthcoming Eurobond, but dealers said on Tuesday both remain vulnerable to political worries.
Dealers saw the spread between MinFins and U.S. Treasuries to narrowing more, but MinFins, which have risen up to two points since the rating news, could also see some profit-taking.
"Prices will rise a bit more...The trend will be more stable and volatility might decrease, said Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault.

The three international rating agencies, IBCA, Standard & Poors and Moody's did not assign investment grade ratings to Russia on Monday, but dealers and economists said the grades in the high speculative range, were better than expected.
IBCA gave Russia BB+ for long-term foreign-currency debt, S&P gave it BB- long-term and Moody's assigned Russia Ba2.

"The ratings are a little bit better than we might have assessed the country vis-a-vis some of the other emerging markets," said Charles Blitzer, chief economist, emerging markets, at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
Russia's BB+ rating puts it on par with Uruguay, just below Hungary, Tunisia and Slovakia and just above Romania, South Africa, Turkey and Brazil, said IBCA managing director Christopher Huhne.
Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said the rating meant Russian debt was a speculative investment.
"It may be seen already that the rise is not feverish, and some London operators are ready to close their positions and take profits," he said.
In the longer run, prices will be heavily influenced by political developments, dealers said.
"Nervousness remains on the market. The risk-involved factor is important now as all MinFin tranches are already heavy (after the rise ahead and on rating news)," Sool said.
President Boris Yeltsin is in the hospital awaiting heart surgery in up to nine weeks' time.
The operation could coincide with the launch of the planned Eurobond, which London bankers expect will be for between $300 and $500 million with a three- to five-year maturity.
"The importance of political news outgoing from Russia will become much stronger once the market digests and gets used to the rating," said Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov.
But if no political problems arise, Rodionov was relatively optimistic about the Eurobond terms and the outlook for MinFins.
"If everything is all right about politics, the U.S. Treasury-Eurobond spread will be at most +400 b.p. and 480-500 b.p. between MinFins and Treasuries," he said.
Eurobank's Coursault was also cautiously optimistic about the Eurobond but saw less growth potential for MinFins.
"Some people think that the spread between the Treasuries and Eurobonds may be around 400 basis points and that with the MinFins 500-600 b.p.," he said.

But Sool saw a 500-600 basis points spread between U.S. Treasuries and Eurobonds, with a spread of 50-100 basis points between Eurobonds and the third 1999 MinFin tranche and 150 basis points between Eurobonds and the fourth 2003 maturity.
